captions: 從開放到封閉的九公分立方體。
包含較小框架的框架立方體。
在板面立方體之中的立方體。
以角落立於另一個立方體內的立方體。

sections.heading: Kindred Volumes - Scale and Confidence in a Simple Form
sections.body: A story heard at bedtime can shape the way space is imagined. Here a tale of a shy cube that finds confidence among companions of its own kind became the starting point for a sequence of studies on the most elementary of volumes. Drawings first explored the cube in one-point and two-point perspective, scattering boxes across the page to observe how edges converge and recede. Small foam cubes were then combined into varied clusters, and one arrangement was developed into a solid stepped model, recorded through top, side, front and back views and through axonometric drawings that clarify how its volumes interlock. The final stage turned to scale and proportion. Twenty-one cubes were built from wooden strips and panels in three sizes, each with a different balance of open frame and closed face. Placing smaller cubes within larger ones tested a playful equation in which three and six combine to make nine. Through these nested frames the project reveals how a simple form gains richness and presence through relationship.

zh-Hant.heading: 相契的量體-簡單形體中的尺度與自信
zh-Hant.body: 一個睡前聽到的故事，可以塑造人們想像空間的方式。在這裡，一個害羞的立方體在同類夥伴之中找到自信的故事，成為一系列以最基本量體為主題的研究起點。繪圖首先以一點與兩點透視探索立方體，把方盒散布在紙面上，觀察邊線如何匯聚與後退。接著小泡棉方塊被組合成多樣的群組，其中一種排列被發展為實心的階梯模型，並透過頂視、側視、正視與背視，以及闡明量體如何相互咬合的軸測圖加以記錄。最後的階段轉向尺度與比例。以木條與板材製作了三種尺寸的二十一個立方體，每一個的開放框架與封閉面都有不同的平衡。把較小的立方體置入較大的立方體之中，測試了一道三與六相加成為九的趣味算式。透過這些嵌套的框架，這個專題揭示一個簡單的形體如何因關係而獲得豐富與存在感。

pins.title: Transforming Composition
pins.description:
Drawings that abstract natural and artificial materials lead to two timber-strip structures, one light and one dense, combined into a frame cube with floating panels.

Physical model and drawing | Composition study | Wooden strips, PVC panels | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 轉化構成
zh-Hant.description:
抽象化自然與人工材料的繪圖，引出兩種木條結構，一輕一密，並組合成一座帶有漂浮板片的框架立方體。

實體模型與繪圖｜構成研究｜木條、PVC板｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Natural and artificial materials found in daily life each carry their own patterns and proportions. The project asked how a flat composition drawn from them could be transformed into a three-dimensional structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 日常生活中的自然與人工材料各自帶有獨特的紋理與比例。這個專題探問，從中提取的平面構成如何能轉化為立體結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Grass, soil, a metal shelf and an outdoor bin were translated into line drawings. The shelf produced strong grids and chevrons, while the ground became a net of triangles.
captions: The ground as a net of triangles.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草、泥土、金屬架與戶外垃圾桶被轉譯為線條繪圖。金屬架產生強烈的網格與人字紋，而地面則化為一張三角形的網。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The planar composition of the shelf was laid out on a grid and built in wooden strips. Two structures were made, one light and clear and the other dense and complex.
captions: Strips laid out on a grid.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 金屬架的平面構成被佈置在網格上，並以木條建造。製作了兩種結構，一種輕盈清晰，另一種密集繁複。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The light structure was turned upside down and set over the dense base to form a single cube. White PVC panels were inserted to float within the frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 輕盈的結構被倒轉，放置在密集的基座之上，形成單一的立方體。白色PVC板被插入，漂浮在框架之中。

sections.heading: Grid and Ground - Everyday Patterns Rebuilt as Space
sections.body: Ordinary surroundings hold a quiet repertoire of patterns, and this project began by noticing them. Flowers and grass, bare soil, a metal shelf glimpsed in a corner and an outdoor bin were each translated into line drawings that stripped away colour and texture to reveal underlying structure. The natural subjects dissolved into restless curves and irregular triangles, while the artificial objects yielded strict grids, repeated verticals and bold chevrons. Among these studies the composition of the shelf proved the most suggestive. Its planar order was laid out on a gridded board and built with fine wooden strips, producing two contrasting structures, one light and clear, the other dense and intricate. Rather than choosing between them, the final model inverted the lighter frame and set it over the denser base, so that openness and complexity meet within a single cube. White panels were inserted at intervals, appearing to hover between the members. The result shows how patterns drawn from the everyday can be rebuilt as layered space.

zh-Hant.heading: 網格與地面-重建為空間的日常紋理
zh-Hant.body: 平凡的周遭蘊藏著一套安靜的紋理，這個專題從注意它們開始。花與草、裸露的泥土、在角落瞥見的金屬架，以及一個戶外垃圾桶，各自被轉譯為線條繪圖，剝除色彩與質感，揭示其底層的結構。自然的對象溶解為躁動的曲線與不規則的三角形，而人工物件則產生嚴謹的網格、重複的垂直線與醒目的人字紋。在這些研究之中，金屬架的構成最具啟發性。它的平面秩序被佈置在有網格的板上，並以細木條建造，產生兩種對比的結構，一種輕盈清晰，另一種密集繁複。最終的模型沒有在兩者之間取捨，而是把較輕的框架倒轉，置於較密的基座之上，使開放與繁複在單一的立方體中相遇。白色板片間隔地插入，彷彿懸浮在構件之間。成果展示了取自日常的紋理如何能被重建為層疊的空間。

pins.title: Transforming a Multifunctional Building
pins.description:
Elements taken from a transforming toy robot become folding card volumes with wooden fasteners, then a translucent frame of acrylic panels and taut lines.

Physical model and sketches | Transformable structure study | Cardboard, wooden fasteners, acrylic panels, strips, thread | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 變形的多功能建築
zh-Hant.description:
取自可變形玩具機器人的元素，化為帶有木製扣件的摺疊卡紙量體，接著發展為由壓克力板與緊繃線條構成的半透明框架。

實體模型與草圖｜可變形結構研究｜卡紙、木製扣件、壓克力板、條材、線｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

captions: The translucent frame of the second model.
第二個模型的半透明框架。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A transforming toy changes its shape and function through rotating joints and simple geometric parts. The project asked how these principles could shape a building that adapts to different uses and sites.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 可變形的玩具透過旋轉的關節與簡單的幾何部件改變形狀與功能。這個專題探問，這些原理如何能塑造一座適應不同用途與基地的建築。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches broke the toy into sharp triangles and lines and studied its rotating attachments. Added parts were drawn as rails and hinges that let the pieces move.
captions: Rails and hinges drawn as added parts.
A drawing of the first model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖把玩具拆解為尖銳的三角形與線條，並研究其旋轉的附件。附加部件被繪製為讓構件得以移動的軌道與鉸鏈。
captions: 繪成附加部件的軌道與鉸鏈。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The first model folded card into angular volumes held by wooden fasteners, which were firmer than tape. Their colour contrasted with the card and made the structure more flexible.
captions: Another view of the card model.
A series of views of the first model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一個模型把卡紙摺成稜角分明的量體，並以比膠帶更牢固的木製扣件固定。扣件的顏色與卡紙形成對比，也使結構更具彈性。
captions: 卡紙模型的另一個視角。
第一個模型的一系列視角。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The second model replaced the card with translucent panels and rebuilt the structure as a frame of strips and taut lines. On land it can transform into many shapes, and on water it can spread out and float.
captions: A folded unit of the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 第二個模型以半透明板取代卡紙，並把結構重建為由條材與緊繃線條構成的框架。在陸地上它能變換為多種形狀，在水面上則能展開並漂浮。

sections.heading: Folding Machine - A Building That Changes Its Shape
sections.body: A toy that transforms from one figure into another offers an unusual lesson in architecture, for its parts must rotate, slide and lock while belonging to one body. This project extracted those principles, focusing on rotating attachments and simple geometric components, and reimagined them as a building able to change function. Early sketches dissolved the toy into sharp triangles and radiating lines, while further drawings proposed rails and hinges as added parts that allow movement. The first model translated these ideas into folded card, its angular volumes held together by wooden fasteners chosen because tape proved too weak. The pale wood contrasted with the card and lent the joints a visible role. A second model then replaced the card entirely, reconstructing the structure as a translucent frame of panels braced by strips and taut lines. Imagined at full scale, the building would reshape itself on land to suit each site and, on water, unfold and float.

zh-Hant.heading: 摺疊的機器-改變形狀的建築
zh-Hant.body: 一個能從一種形象變換為另一種形象的玩具，為建築提供了一堂不尋常的課，因為它的部件必須旋轉、滑動與鎖定，卻同屬一體。這個專題提取這些原理，聚焦於旋轉的附件與簡單的幾何部件，並把它們重新想像為一座能夠改變功能的建築。早期的草圖把玩具溶解為尖銳的三角形與放射的線條，進一步的繪圖則提出軌道與鉸鏈作為讓運動成為可能的附加部件。第一個模型把這些構想轉譯為摺疊的卡紙，稜角分明的量體以木製扣件固定，選擇扣件是因為膠帶被證明太過薄弱。淺色的木材與卡紙形成對比，使接點扮演明顯的角色。第二個模型接著完全取代了卡紙，把結構重建為由板片構成、以條材與緊繃線條支撐的半透明框架。若以實際尺度想像，這座建築能在陸地上重塑自身以適應每個基地，並在水面上展開漂浮。

pins.title: Replan and Joint Bridge
pins.description:
Observation of a busy station district leads to a curving bridge that separates cyclists and walkers while offering steps for rest, shade and conversation.

Physical model and sketches | Urban connector design | Cardboard, white board, scale figures | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 重新規劃的連接橋
zh-Hant.description:
對一個繁忙車站街區的觀察，引出一座彎曲的橋，它分隔騎車者與步行者，同時提供可以休息、遮陰與交談的階梯。

實體模型與草圖｜城市連接體設計｜卡紙、白色板材、比例人偶｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

captions: The bridge model with figures resting on its steps.
人偶在階梯上休息的橋梁模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Near a busy railway station a park was divided into many parts, which kept people apart and made the long wait to cross the road troublesome. The project asked how a bridge could improve transport while also giving people a place to rest and communicate.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在一個繁忙的火車站附近，一座公園被分割為許多部分，使人們彼此疏離，等待過馬路的時間也冗長而麻煩。這個專題探問，一座橋如何能改善交通，同時為人們提供休息與交流的地方。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The movements of residents and travellers were observed, from cycling and walking to resting in the shade. Shortcomings were identified, including cyclists colliding with walkers and the lack of shelter from strong sun.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究觀察了居民與旅客的活動，從騎車、步行到在陰涼處休息。研究辨識出種種缺點，包括騎車者與步行者相撞，以及缺乏遮擋強烈陽光的遮蔽。
captions: 騎車者與步行者的路線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stepped platforms were sketched as places to sit and talk, and sloped walls were tested as shade. Separate curving lanes were drawn so that bicycles and people would not cross.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 階梯狀的平台被繪製為可以坐下交談的地方，斜牆則被測試作為遮陰。草圖畫出分開的彎曲通道，使自行車與行人不再交錯。
captions: 作為遮陰而測試的斜牆。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final bridge branches and curves, with rows of steps where figures relax, gather and shelter from the sun. Gentle slopes allow travellers to pull luggage easily while cyclists keep to their own lane.
captions: A long curve of the bridge.
Seats sheltered by a raised edge.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的橋梁分岔而彎曲，一排排階梯讓人偶在其中放鬆、聚集並躲避陽光。和緩的坡道讓旅客能輕鬆拉著行李，騎車者則保持在自己的車道上。
captions: 由升起的邊緣遮蔽的座位。

sections.heading: Bridge as Plaza - Movement and Pause Above the Street
sections.body: A bridge is usually measured by how quickly it carries people across, yet this project asked what it might offer to those who linger. Beside a busy railway station, a park had been divided into fragments, keeping neighbours apart and forcing long waits at the crossing, while strong sun left few places to shelter. Careful observation recorded the rhythms of residents and travellers, people cycling, wandering, enjoying the cool shade and hurrying with luggage toward their trains. From these notes a set of strategies emerged, addressing communication, shade, safe separation and convenience. Sketches developed stepped platforms where people could sit and talk, sloped walls that cast shadow, and parallel curving lanes that keep bicycles and pedestrians from colliding. The model draws these ideas into a single branching structure in white board. Rows of steps hold small figures relaxing and gathering, raised edges shelter seats from the sun, and gentle slopes ease the passage of luggage. The bridge becomes an elevated plaza where movement and pause can coexist.

zh-Hant.heading: 作為廣場的橋-街道之上的移動與停留
zh-Hant.body: 一座橋通常以它多快把人送到對岸來衡量，這個專題卻探問它能為那些逗留的人提供什麼。在一個繁忙的火車站旁，一座公園被分割成片段，使鄰里彼此疏離，也迫使人們在路口長時間等待，而強烈的陽光讓可以遮蔽的地方寥寥無幾。細心的觀察記錄了居民與旅客的節奏，有人騎車，有人閒逛，有人享受陰涼，也有人拖著行李趕往火車。從這些紀錄中浮現出一組策略，回應交流、遮陰、安全分隔與便利。草圖發展出可以讓人坐下交談的階梯平台、投下陰影的斜牆，以及讓自行車與行人不再相撞的平行彎曲通道。模型以白色板材把這些構想匯聚為單一的分岔結構。一排排階梯承載著放鬆與聚集的小人偶，升起的邊緣為座位遮擋陽光，和緩的坡道讓行李的通行更輕鬆。這座橋成為一個高架廣場，讓移動與停留得以共存。

pins.title: Tower and Space
pins.description:
Four storeys of a slender tower of grids, cardboard and ropes each tell a separate story, showing difference and harmony across changing scales.

Physical model | Scale and narrative study | Cardboard, wooden strips, PVC boards, linen ropes | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 塔與空間
zh-Hant.description:
一座由網格、紙板與繩索構成的纖細高塔，四個樓層各自講述一個獨立的故事，展現在變化尺度之間的差異與和諧。

實體模型｜尺度與敘事研究｜紙板、木條、PVC板、亞麻繩｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The same world looks entirely different when viewed at very different scales. The project asked how a single tower could hold four independent stories while remaining one harmonious whole.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 同一個世界在截然不同的尺度下觀看時，看起來完全不同。這個專題探問，一座塔如何能容納四個獨立的故事，同時仍是一個和諧的整體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A sequence of images zooming from a vast landscape to the texture of skin was studied for its jumps in scale. Four short literary passages were then chosen, each suggesting a different mood for one floor.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究分析了一組從遼闊地景一路放大到皮膚紋理的圖像，觀察其中尺度的跳躍。接著選擇了四段簡短的文學片段，各自為一個樓層暗示不同的氛圍。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The first floor became a labyrinth of walls seen through a grid, and the second a cluster of white blocks. The third floor raised stairs and ropes toward a high point, and each level was framed by wooden strips.
captions: The labyrinth of the first floor.
White blocks of the second floor.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一層成為透過網格看見的牆體迷宮，第二層則是一簇白色的塊體。第三層把階梯與繩索升向高處，每一層都以木條框起。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The fourth floor holds a small solitary chamber within a translucent pyramid. Stacked together, the four floors show difference and harmony across scales.
captions: Stairs and ropes of the third floor.
The chamber of the fourth floor.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 第四層在半透明的角錐中容納一個孤獨的小房間。四個樓層疊合在一起，展現跨越尺度的差異與和諧。

sections.heading: Stacked Worlds - Four Stories Within One Tower
sections.body: The same world can appear utterly different when observed from far away or from very close, and this project explored how such shifts of scale might be gathered into a single vertical structure. A sequence of images that travels from an expansive landscape down to the fine texture of skin served as the initial reference, revealing how each leap in scale produces a new kind of space. Four brief literary passages were then selected, each evoking a distinct emotional condition, and every floor of the tower was assigned one of them. The lowest level became a labyrinth of walls glimpsed through a dense grid, recalling a journey of sorrow and remembrance. The second gathered white blocks around an empty centre, suggesting time that circles rather than advances. The third lifted stairs and ropes toward a precarious summit, and the highest enclosed a solitary chamber within a translucent pyramid. Framed by slender wooden strips, the four worlds are stacked into one tower, where difference and harmony are held in balance.

zh-Hant.heading: 疊合的世界-一座塔中的四個故事
zh-Hant.body: 同一個世界從遠處或極近處觀看時，可以顯得截然不同，這個專題探索如何把這樣的尺度轉換匯聚為單一的垂直結構。一組從遼闊地景一路深入到皮膚細緻紋理的圖像，作為最初的參考，揭示每一次尺度的跳躍如何產生一種新的空間。接著選擇了四段簡短的文學片段，各自喚起一種獨特的情感狀態，塔的每一層都被賦予其中之一。最低的一層成為透過密集網格瞥見的牆體迷宮，令人想起一段悲傷與追憶的旅程。第二層把白色塊體聚集在空蕩的中心周圍，暗示一種環繞而非前進的時間。第三層把階梯與繩索升向一個危險的頂點，最高的一層則在半透明的角錐中圍合出一個孤獨的房間。在纖細木條的框架中，這四個世界被疊合為一座塔，差異與和諧在其中保持平衡。

pins.title: Space and Structure
pins.description:
Sticks, foam and board are tested as line, block and plane, then linear plans are layered into a card model whose levels are refined and opened to light.

Physical model and drawing | Space and structure study | Card paper, wooden sticks, foam | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 空間與結構
zh-Hant.description:
木棒、泡棉與板材被測試為線、塊與面，接著線性平面被層疊為一座卡紙模型，其樓層經過精簡，並向光線敞開。

實體模型與繪圖｜空間與結構研究｜卡紙、木棒、泡棉｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

captions: The final model of linear planes.
線性平面構成的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Line, block and plane can each define space, yet they rarely work alone in a building. The project asked how a limited set of materials could create many different spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 線、塊與面各自都能界定空間，但在建築中它們很少單獨運作。這個專題探問，一組有限的材料如何能創造多種不同的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sticks, blue foam and paper board were first used alone and then combined into basic structures. Linear plans proved an interesting language, as lines crossing vertically or in parallel could create different levels.
captions: A refined model of frames and blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 木棒、藍色泡棉與紙板先被單獨使用，再組合成基本結構。線性平面被證明是一種有趣的語言，因為垂直或平行交錯的線條能創造不同的層次。
captions: 框架與塊體的深化模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Preliminary boards tested linear plans with foam blocks, and refined models raised the ground plan to follow upper levels. The many levels proved unnecessary, which led to an improved model.
captions: An interior view of the spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 初步的底板以泡棉塊測試線性平面，深化模型則讓地面平面跟隨上層的結構。過多的樓層被證明並不必要，因而促成了改良的模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model keeps the linear language but reduces the plans to one or two levels. Transparent planes were added so that light passes through and the inner spaces can be seen clearly.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型保留了線性語言，但把平面精簡為一到兩層。加入的透明平面讓光線穿透，也讓內部空間得以清楚看見。

sections.heading: Lines Becoming Rooms - Clarity Through Reduction
sections.body: Architecture may be understood as a meeting of art and science, and this project approached that meeting through the most basic means. Sticks, blue foam and paper board were first explored as line, block and plane, each used alone before being combined into small structures. From these experiments a single idea emerged with unusual force, that linear plans, lines drawn on the ground and raised into thin walls, could generate surprisingly rich space when they cross vertically or run in parallel. Preliminary boards tested such plans together with foam blocks, and refined models raised the ground plan so that it followed the structure of levels above. Yet the abundance of levels began to confuse rather than enrich, and this recognition guided the final model. Here the linear language is retained but restrained to one or two levels, while transparent planes are inserted among the walls. Light now passes into the interior and its spaces can be read with clarity, demonstrating how reduction can sharpen a design.

zh-Hant.heading: 化為房間的線-透過精簡獲得清晰
zh-Hant.body: 建築可以被理解為藝術與科學的交會，這個專題透過最基本的手段接近這樣的交會。木棒、藍色泡棉與紙板首先被探索為線、塊與面，各自單獨使用，然後再組合成小型結構。從這些實驗中浮現出一個格外有力的想法，線性平面，也就是畫在地面上、再升起為薄牆的線條，在垂直交錯或平行延伸時，能產生出人意料的豐富空間。初步的底板把這樣的平面與泡棉塊一起測試，深化模型則讓地面平面跟隨上方樓層的結構。然而樓層的繁多開始造成混亂而非豐富，這樣的體認引導了最終的模型。在這裡，線性語言被保留，卻收斂為一到兩層，透明的平面則被插入牆體之間。光線如今進入內部，空間得以被清晰地閱讀，展示了精簡如何能使設計更加銳利。

pins.title: Linear Structure
pins.description:
Hundreds of parallel lines drawn on transparent paper are raised as card walls of varying height, so a light board beneath glows through them in different strengths.

Physical model and drawing | Linear structure study | Card paper, transparent paper, model trees, light board | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 線性結構
zh-Hant.description:
畫在透明紙上的數百條平行線被升起為高度不一的卡紙牆，讓下方的發光板以不同的強度透過它們發光。

實體模型與繪圖｜線性結構研究｜卡紙、透明紙、模型樹、發光板｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

captions: The field of card walls lit from below.
由下方照亮的卡紙牆場域。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A single structure or pattern, used on its own, can still produce many interesting spaces. The project asked whether a model built only from lines and planes could create a rich landscape.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 單一的結構或圖樣即使單獨使用，仍能產生許多有趣的空間。這個專題探問，一個只由線與面構成的模型能否創造豐富的地景。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Inspired by a linear elevated park, many lines of different lengths were drawn in parallel on transparent paper. The concept drawing became a dense field of strokes.
captions: A concept drawing of parallel lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 受一座線性高架公園啟發，許多長度不一的線條被平行地畫在透明紙上。這張概念圖成為一片密集的筆觸場域。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Following the length of each line, card was cut to different heights and set on the paper. Model trees were placed among the walls to give a sense of scale.
captions: The field of walls and trees.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 依循每條線的長度，卡紙被切成不同的高度並立在紙上。模型樹被放置在牆體之間，以提供尺度感。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A light board placed beneath the transparent paper makes the model glow. The light passes through with different strengths because of the different heights of the planes.
captions: The skyline of walls and trees.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 放在透明紙下方的發光板使模型發光。由於面的高度各異，光線以不同的強度穿透。

sections.heading: Glowing Lines - A Landscape Drawn in Light
sections.body: A single structural idea, pursued with discipline, can yield a surprising variety of space, and this project tested that belief using nothing more than lines and planes. Taking cues from a linear elevated park, it began with a concept drawing in which countless lines of differing lengths run parallel across a sheet of transparent paper, their density shifting like grass in wind. Each line was then translated directly into form. Card was cut to a height that followed the length of its line and stood upright on the paper, so that the drawing rose into a field of thin walls, some low enough to step over, others tall enough to enclose a path. Small model trees were placed among them to establish scale and to suggest a park through which visitors might wander. The decisive move was to set a light board beneath the transparent base. Light now rises through the field, filtered more or less strongly by planes of different heights, and the drawing becomes a luminous landscape.

zh-Hant.heading: 發光的線-以光繪出的地景
zh-Hant.body: 一個以紀律追求的單一結構構想，可以產生出人意料的多樣空間，這個專題僅以線與面來檢驗這樣的信念。從一座線性高架公園得到啟發，研究從一張概念圖開始，無數長度不一的線條平行地橫越一張透明紙，其密度如風中的草般變化。每一條線接著被直接轉譯為形體。卡紙被切成與線條長度相應的高度，直立在紙上，使這張圖升起為一片薄牆的場域，有些低得可以跨過，有些則高得足以圍合一條小徑。小型模型樹被放置在其間，以建立尺度，並暗示一座讓訪客可以漫步其中的公園。關鍵的一步是在透明的底面下放置一塊發光板。光線如今穿過整個場域向上升起，被高度各異的面或強或弱地過濾，這張圖便成為一片明亮的地景。

pins.title: Triangles Structure
pins.description:
Random shapes traced from natural textures are reduced to triangles, built as stick pyramids and extended across a ground plan into a towering frame.

Physical model and drawing | Structure study | Museum board, wooden sticks, card paper, model trees | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 三角結構
zh-Hant.description:
從自然紋理描摹的隨機形狀被簡化為三角形，建成木棒角錐，再沿著地面平面延伸為一座高聳的框架。

實體模型與繪圖｜結構研究｜博物館紙板、木棒、卡紙、模型樹｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

captions: 三角形構成的高聳框架。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Linear plans alone could not create enough different spaces. The project asked which other structure could offer a stronger sense of space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 單靠線性平面無法創造足夠多樣的空間。這個專題探問，還有哪一種結構能提供更強的空間感。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Many random shapes were drawn following the textures in a set of photographs. Among them the triangle proved the most orderly and gave the strongest sense of space.
captions: A study of strokes from a texture.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 許多隨機形狀依循一組照片中的紋理被描繪出來。其中三角形被證明最有秩序，也帶來最強的空間感。
captions: 從紋理提取的筆觸研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Triangles were cut out and wooden sticks of different lengths were glued to their edges to form pyramids. These basic units could clearly extend in any direction.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 三角形被切下，不同長度的木棒被黏在它們的邊緣，形成角錐。這些基本單元顯然能向任何方向延伸。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The units were placed on a ground plan and extended with more sticks into a large frame. With only triangles, a great variety of spaces formed above trees and paths.
captions: A low view under the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些單元被放置在地面平面上，並以更多木棒延伸為一座大型框架。僅僅透過三角形，在樹木與小徑之上便形成了豐富多樣的空間。
captions: 框架下方的低角度視角。

sections.heading: Order From Chance - Triangles That Learn to Grow
sections.body: When a sequence of linear plans failed to yield enough variety, this project turned elsewhere for a structural language. It began by drawing random shapes that followed the textures of a set of photographs, letting brushy strokes and scattered marks accumulate across the page. From this apparently chaotic material a single figure stood out. The triangle, the most stable and orderly of shapes, produced the strongest sense of space, and a dense net of triangles was drawn to explore its possibilities. The figures were then cut out and wooden sticks of varying lengths were glued to their edges, lifting each flat triangle into a slender pyramid. Building several of these units revealed a crucial property, that the structure could extend freely in any direction. A ground plan was therefore prepared, the units were set upon it and further sticks were added to link them, until a towering lattice rose above model trees and paths. With a single geometric rule, an astonishing diversity of enclosed and open spaces emerged.

zh-Hant.heading: 偶然中的秩序-學會生長的三角形
zh-Hant.body: 當一系列線性平面無法產生足夠的變化時，這個專題轉向別處尋找結構語言。研究從描繪隨機形狀開始，這些形狀依循一組照片的紋理，讓刷痕般的筆觸與散落的記號在紙面上累積。從這些看似混亂的材料中，一個形狀脫穎而出。三角形是最穩定、最有秩序的形狀，它帶來最強的空間感，於是一張密集的三角網被繪製出來，探索它的可能性。這些形狀接著被切下，長度不一的木棒被黏在它們的邊緣，把每一個平面三角形升起為纖細的角錐。製作數個這樣的單元之後，一個關鍵的特性顯現出來，這種結構能夠自由地向任何方向延伸。於是準備了一張地面平面，單元被放置其上，再加入更多木棒把它們連結起來，直到一座高聳的格架在模型樹與小徑之上升起。僅憑一條幾何規則，便浮現出令人驚嘆的多樣圍合與開放空間。

pins.title: Shoes Exploration
pins.description:
Sneakers are sketched and taken apart to find their structures, and the wavy spaces they reveal grow into a park of curved sheets around a spiral tower.

Physical model and sketches | Object deconstruction study | PVC, card paper, iron wire, rope, wooden sticks, museum board | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 鞋的探索
zh-Hant.description:
運動鞋被描繪並拆解以尋找其結構，它們所揭示的波浪狀空間，發展為一座環繞螺旋塔、由彎曲薄片構成的公園。

實體模型與草圖｜物件解構研究｜PVC、卡紙、鐵絲、繩子、木棒、博物館紙板｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A sneaker is assembled from many layered parts that wrap the foot in curving forms. The project asked what kinds of space could be discovered by taking such objects apart.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一隻運動鞋由許多層疊的部件組成，以彎曲的形態包覆雙腳。這個專題探問，拆解這樣的物件能發現哪些種類的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Several sneakers were studied and drawn in continuous overlapping lines, and one pair was dismantled to reveal its layers. Shaded sketches then analysed the hollow spaces formed by the curving parts.
captions: A shaded analysis of hollow space.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究分析並以連續交疊的線條描繪了數隻運動鞋，其中一雙被拆解以揭示其層次。帶陰影的草圖接著分析了彎曲部件所形成的中空空間。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Process models curled white strips into loops and waves to test these hollow spaces. The spaces formed by wavy elements became the theme of the final model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 過程模型把白色條帶捲成環圈與波浪，以測試這些中空空間。由波浪狀元素形成的空間成為最終模型的主題。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model combines paper, sticks, transparent sheets, strings and wire into a park with a tower. Wavy surfaces connect the tower with the surrounding shelter, and spiral stairs rise beneath wire arches.
captions: The spiral stair of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型結合紙張、木棒、透明片、繩子與鐵絲，形成一座帶有塔的公園。波浪狀的表面連結塔與周圍的遮蔽空間，螺旋階梯在鐵絲拱下升起。

sections.heading: Unlaced Forms - Wavy Spaces Drawn From Footwear
sections.body: An everyday object can conceal a surprising architecture, and this project uncovered one inside the familiar sneaker. Several pairs were studied and drawn in continuous, overlapping lines. One pair was then carefully dismantled, revealing a sequence of layered parts, each curving to wrap and support the foot. Shaded sketches analysed the hollows formed between these parts, recording how wavy surfaces fold to make shelter. Process models translated these findings into curled white strips, looping and overlapping to form pockets of enclosed space. Encouraged by the beauty of these wavy forms, the final model gathered as many materials as possible, combining paper, sticks, transparent sheets, strings and iron wire into a small park with a tower at its heart. Broad curved surfaces sweep outward to link the tower with a surrounding shelter, while timber treads spiral upward beneath delicate arches of wire. The resulting landscape appears almost natural, its fluid order discovered within an ordinary shoe.

zh-Hant.heading: 鬆開的形體-取自鞋履的波浪空間
zh-Hant.body: 一件日常物品可以隱藏著令人驚訝的建築，這個專題在熟悉的運動鞋之中發現了一座。研究分析了數雙鞋，並以連續交疊的線條加以描繪。其中一雙接著被仔細拆解，揭示出一連串層疊的部件，每一件都彎曲著包覆並支撐雙腳。帶陰影的草圖分析了這些部件之間形成的凹處，記錄波浪狀的表面如何摺疊成為遮蔽。過程模型把這些發現轉譯為捲曲的白色條帶，它們迴繞交疊，形成一個個圍合的空間口袋。受到這些波浪形態之美的鼓舞，最終模型集結了盡可能多的材料，結合紙張、木棒、透明片、繩子與鐵絲，形成一座以塔為核心的小公園。寬闊的彎曲表面向外延展，把塔與周圍的遮蔽空間連結起來，木製踏階則在纖細的鐵絲拱下螺旋上升。完成的地景幾乎顯得自然，它流動的秩序是在一隻平凡的鞋中被發現的。

pins.title: Tree Houses
pins.description:
Rather than a single house, stairs and terraces follow the flow of real branches set on a dark base, so that resting places climb through the tree.

Physical model and drawing | Nature and structure study | Rope, wooden sticks, wooden board, branches | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 樹屋
zh-Hant.description:
這個專題並非建造單一的房屋，而是讓階梯與平台沿著立在深色底座上的真實樹枝流動，使休憩的地方穿越樹木向上攀升。

實體模型與繪圖｜自然與結構研究｜繩子、木棒、木板、樹枝｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

captions: The tree house model of branches and terraces.
樹枝與平台構成的樹屋模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Many tree houses blend with nature because they follow the structure and lines of the trees that hold them. The project asked how a place for rest could be built without cutting or forcing the branches.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 許多樹屋能融入自然，是因為它們依循承托它們的樹木的結構與線條。這個專題探問，如何能在不砍斷也不扭曲樹枝的情況下，建造一個休憩的地方。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Concept drawings placed small platforms, stairs and joints between trunks and branches. Stairs were seen as the best way to show changes of level.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 概念圖把小型平台、階梯與接點放置在樹幹與枝條之間。階梯被視為表現高度變化的最佳方式。
captions: 樹枝與平台之間的接點。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: An elevation drawing layered stairs, rooms and terraces along the flowing lines of the tree. Real branches were then bound together as the main frame instead of many supporting sticks.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一張立面圖沿著樹木流動的線條層疊了階梯、房間與平台。接著真實的樹枝被綁紮在一起作為主要框架，取代大量的支撐木棒。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final model the branches carry all the stairs and terraces, and figures rest at every level. Set on a dark rocky base, the structure looks like part of nature.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最終模型中，樹枝承載著所有的階梯與平台，人偶在每一層休息。立在深色的岩石狀底座上，這個結構看起來宛如自然的一部分。

sections.heading: Following the Branch - Stairs That Grow Through a Tree
sections.body: The most convincing tree houses seem to grow from their hosts, following the structure and lines of the trees that carry them rather than imposing a separate order. This project took that observation as its guiding principle and set aside the idea of a single enclosed house. Instead it proposed a vertical sequence of places for rest, linked by stairs, because stairs most clearly express a change of level. Concept drawings scattered small platforms between trunks, traced flights of steps along rising branches and studied the joints where timber meets bark. An elevation drawing then layered rooms, terraces and stairs into a dense composition that follows the flowing lines of the tree without cutting any limb. In the model, real branches were bound together with rope to form the primary frame, replacing the many supporting sticks a conventional structure would require. Stairs and terraces climb along these branches above a dark rocky base, and small figures pause at every level, making a dwelling that feels like a natural extension of the tree.

zh-Hant.heading: 依循枝條-穿越樹木生長的階梯
zh-Hant.body: 最令人信服的樹屋似乎是從它們的宿主長出來的，它們依循承載它們的樹木的結構與線條，而不是強加一種獨立的秩序。這個專題把這樣的觀察作為指導原則，並擱置了單一封閉房屋的構想。取而代之的是一組垂直排列的休憩地點，以階梯相連，因為階梯最能清楚地表達高度的變化。概念圖把小型平台散布在樹幹之間，沿著上升的枝條描繪一段段階梯，並研究木材與樹皮相接的接點。一張立面圖接著把房間、平台與階梯層疊為一個密集的構成，它依循樹木流動的線條，而不砍斷任何枝幹。在模型中，真實的樹枝以繩子綁紮在一起，形成主要框架，取代傳統結構所需要的大量支撐木棒。階梯與平台在深色的岩石狀底座之上沿著這些枝條攀升，小人偶在每一層駐足，構成一處宛如樹木自然延伸的居所。

pins.title: Lifted Triangles
pins.description:
A photograph is traced into a mesh of triangles, built in wooden sticks on a printed board, then released and lifted into a towering cage of sticks and paper planes.

Physical model and drawing | 2D to 3D transformation study | Wooden sticks, paper | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 升起的三角形
zh-Hant.description:
一張照片被描繪成三角形網格，以木棒在印好的紙板上建構，再被釋放並抬升為一座由木棒與紙片構成的高聳籠狀構造。

實體模型與繪圖｜平面到立體的轉化研究｜木棒、紙｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

captions: The final tower of sticks and paper planes.
木棒與紙片構成的最終塔體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A flat image has no thickness, yet it can hold a pattern that suggests structure. The project asked how a drawing on paper could be built up into a form that can be touched and explored.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 平面圖像沒有厚度，卻能承載暗示結構的圖案。這個專題探問，一張紙上的圖如何能被建構成一個可以觸摸與探索的形體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A photograph taken by the student was traced into a mesh of irregular triangles, chosen because the triangle is the most stable structural figure. The line drawing was printed onto paperboard so that every line could guide the placement of a stick.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生自己拍攝的一張照片被描繪成不規則的三角形網格，選擇三角形是因為它是最穩定的結構圖形。這張線條圖被印在紙板上，讓每一條線都能引導一根木棒的位置。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden sticks were glued along the printed lines and the blank areas between them were cut away. The released mesh became a flexible platform that could be bent, folded and lifted into three dimensions.
captions: The mesh lifted into three dimensions.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木棒沿著印出的線條黏合，線條之間的空白區域則被切除。被釋放的網格成為一個柔韌的平台，可以彎曲、摺疊並抬升為立體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model rises as a dense cage of triangles, with paper planes inserted at varying angles and small figures placed among them. Under directed light the lines cast intricate shadows, while the layered waves suggest different stories and the complexity of society.
captions: A low view of the model.
A close view of the triangles.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型升起為一座密集的三角形籠狀構造，紙片以不同角度插入，小人偶散布其間。在定向光線下，線條投下繁複的影子，層疊的波浪則暗示不同的故事與社會的複雜。

sections.heading: Paper Mesh Rising - Shadows of Stable Lines
sections.body: Every built form begins, in some sense, as a flat image, and this project made that passage its explicit subject. A photograph was traced into an irregular net of triangles, the most stable figure available to a builder, so that the resulting drawing already carried a latent structure within its lines. Printed onto paperboard, the drawing became a template: wooden sticks were glued along each line and the empty fields between them were cut away, releasing a mesh that could bend and fold without losing coherence. What had been a picture now behaved like a material. Lifted and gathered, the mesh grew into a towering cage in which paper planes were inserted at shifting angles, catching light and closing certain cells while leaving others open. Small figures inhabit the interior, giving scale to a landscape of ridges and hollows. Under directed light the sticks throw dense shadows across the ground, a second drawing produced by the first. The model thus reads as a meditation on thickness, showing how a line, once given depth, begins to shelter, divide and narrate.

zh-Hant.heading: 紙網升起-穩定線條的影子
zh-Hant.body: 每一個被建造的形體，在某種意義上都始於一幅平面的圖像，這個專題正以這段轉化為主題。一張照片被描繪成一張不規則的三角形網格，三角形最為穩定，因此線條中早已隱含結構。圖面被印在紙板上，成為一個模板，木棒沿著每一條線黏合，線條之間的空白則被切除，釋放出一張能彎曲、能摺疊卻不失整體性的網。原本的圖像於是開始像一種材料般運作。網格被抬升、收攏，長成一座高聳的籠狀構造，紙片以不斷變化的角度插入其中，捕捉光線，封閉某些格子，同時讓其他格子保持敞開。小人偶棲居於內部。在定向光線下，木棒在地面投下濃密的影子，那是由第一張圖所生成的第二張圖。這座模型因此可以被讀作一段關於厚度的沉思，揭示一條線一旦獲得深度，便開始遮蔽、分隔與敘事。

pins.title: Music Wave
pins.description:
Recorded sound waves and light traces are translated into fanned sticks and curled paper, then combined into a refined model of ribbons looping through clusters of sticks.

Physical model and drawing | Sound and form study | Wooden sticks, paper, wire | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 音樂波浪
zh-Hant.description:
錄下的聲波與光軌被轉譯為扇形木棒與捲曲紙片，再結合為一座紙帶在木棒束之間迴旋的深化模型。

實體模型與繪圖｜聲音與形式研究｜木棒、紙、鐵絲｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

captions: The refined model of sticks and paper ribbons.
木棒與紙帶構成的深化模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Sound is invisible, yet a recording reveals waves with rhythm, density and shape. The project asked whether these waves could be translated into a physical structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 聲音是看不見的，但一段錄音能揭示具有節奏、密度與形狀的波動。這個專題探問，這些波動能否被轉譯為一個實體的結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Recorded waveforms were studied alongside sketches and long-exposure light traces that drew the movement of sound in the air. The traces showed loops and twists rather than simple peaks, suggesting forms that coil through space.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 錄下的波形與草圖，以及描繪聲音在空氣中移動的長時間曝光光軌一同被研究。光軌呈現的是迴圈與扭轉，而非單純的波峰，暗示著在空間中盤繞的形式。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Initial models explored three forms, one fanning wooden sticks into a rolling wave and others curling strips of paper into open shells. Each tested how sticks, card and wire could express the flexibility of a wave.
captions: An initial model of fanned sticks.
An initial model of curled paper.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 初步模型探索了三種形式，其中一個把木棒展開成翻滾的波浪，其他則把紙條捲成敞開的殼體。每一個模型都測試木棒、卡紙與鐵絲如何表達波動的柔韌。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The refined model combined the three initial ideas within a frame large enough to hold it. Paper ribbons loop between clusters of wooden sticks, so that the composition reads as the shape of sound itself.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 深化模型把三個初步構想結合在一個足以容納它的框架之中。紙帶在一束束木棒之間迴旋，使整個構成讀起來就像聲音本身的形狀。

sections.heading: Listening With the Hands - Ribbons of Sound
sections.body: Sound occupies space without ever appearing in it, and this project set out to give that invisible occupant a body. Recorded waveforms supplied a first portrait, dense bands of peaks and troughs, but long-exposure traces of light revealed something less orderly: loops, knots and sweeping curves that suggested a wave moves through the air rather than along a line. Sketches followed these coils, and three initial models tested different translations. In one, wooden sticks fan out in a rolling sequence, their regular spacing echoing the pulse of a beat; in others, strips of paper curl into open shells that hold shadow like a resonant cavity. Each material carried a distinct temperament, sticks articulating rhythm while paper expressed continuity. The refined model gathered these temperaments within a frame large enough to contain them. Ribbons swing between bundles of crossing sticks, so that sharp accents and long sustained tones coexist in one suspended structure. The result is less a representation of a particular piece than an instrument for seeing, where listening becomes a matter of form, interval and light.

zh-Hant.heading: 用手聆聽-聲音的紙帶
zh-Hant.body: 聲音佔據空間，卻從不在其中顯現，這個專題試圖為它賦予身體。錄下的波形提供了第一幅肖像，但長時間曝光的光軌卻揭露出較不規則的面貌，包括迴圈、結點與大幅擺盪的曲線，暗示波動是在空氣中穿行，而非沿著一條線前進。草圖追隨這些盤繞的軌跡，三個初步模型則測試不同的轉譯方式。其中一個以木棒展開成連續翻滾的扇形，規律的間距呼應節拍的脈動；其他模型則把紙條捲成敞開的殼體。每一種材料都帶有獨特的性格，木棒表達節奏，紙片則表達連續。深化模型把這些性格收攏在一個足以容納它們的框架之中。紙帶在交錯的木棒束之間擺盪，使尖銳的重音與綿長的延音共存於同一個懸浮的結構。最終的成果與其說是某首樂曲的再現，不如說是一件用來觀看的樂器，讓聆聽成為形式、間隔與光線的問題。

pins.title: Electronic World
pins.description:
The layout of a circuit board is sketched and read as a city plan, then built in straws, sticks, card, foam and screws as towers gathered around a central core.

Physical model and drawing | Urban analogy study | Straws, wooden sticks, white card, foam, screws | Student Project | Design Director: Yu Chun Tsai (full-cycle supervision)

zh-Hant.title: 電子世界
zh-Hant.description:
一塊電路板的配置被描繪下來並當作城市平面閱讀，再以吸管、木棒、卡紙、泡棉與螺絲建構為圍繞中央核心的塔樓群。

實體模型與繪圖｜城市類比研究｜吸管、木棒、白卡紙、泡棉、螺絲｜學生作品｜設計總監 Yu Chun Tsai，全程指導

captions: The city model with its core towers.
帶有核心塔樓的城市模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A city runs on departments, companies and services, much as a circuit board runs on power, a core, memory and circuits. The project asked whether the logic of a circuit board could organise a city.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座城市依靠各種部門、公司與服務運作，就像一塊電路板依靠電源、核心、記憶體與線路運作。這個專題探問，電路板的邏輯能否用來組織一座城市。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The layout of a circuit board was sketched, scanned and redrawn as lines and shapes. Each component was read as an urban function, with circuit lines becoming connections between districts.
captions: A sketch traced from a circuit board.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一塊電路板的配置被描繪、掃描，並重繪為線條與形狀。每一個元件都被讀作一種城市機能，線路則成為街區之間的連結。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The drawn lines were built up with straws, wooden sticks, white card, foam and screws. Different materials identified different functions, while lines tied every department back to the core.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 描繪的線條以吸管、木棒、白色卡紙、泡棉與螺絲建構起來。不同的材料標示不同的機能，線條則把每一個部門繫回核心。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model gathers tall towers around a central core, with low blocks and paths spreading across the board. Small figures move along the connections, showing a city that runs like a circuit.
captions: A side view of the city model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型把高聳的塔樓聚集在中央核心周圍，低矮的街區與路徑則在底板上蔓延。小人偶沿著連結移動，呈現一座像電路般運作的城市。

sections.heading: Currents Becoming Streets - The City as Circuit
sections.body: Analogies between machines and cities are old, yet this project tested one with unusual literalness. A circuit board was treated as a plan: its core became a civic centre, its memory and power units became districts, and the fine traces linking them became streets and lines of service. The board was sketched by hand, scanned and redrawn, so that the drawing preserved both the precision of the original and the hesitations of a hand learning its pattern. Translation into a model required a vocabulary of materials, and here difference itself carried meaning. Straws, wooden sticks, white card, foam and screws each marked a distinct function, allowing a viewer to read the city as an assembly of systems rather than a uniform mass. Towers of stacked plates and threaded columns rise around the core, low blocks spread outward, and taut lines bind every department back to the centre. Small figures populate the routes between them. The resulting landscape suggests that a city, like a circuit, depends less on any single building than on the continuity of its connections.

zh-Hant.heading: 化為街道的電流-作為電路的城市
zh-Hant.body: 把機器與城市相互類比由來已久，這個專題則直接檢驗了其中一個。一塊電路板被當作一張平面圖來閱讀，它的核心成為市民中心，記憶體與電源單元成為不同的街區，連接它們的細密線路則成為街道與服務的路徑。電路板先以手繪描下，再經掃描與重繪，保留了原物的精確與手的遲疑。轉譯為模型需要一套材料的語彙，而在這裡，差異本身就承載著意義。吸管、木棒、白色卡紙、泡棉與螺絲各自標示一種機能，讓觀者能把城市讀作一組系統的集合，而不是一團均質的量體。由層疊板片與螺紋柱構成的塔樓圍繞核心升起，低矮的街區向外蔓延，繃緊的線條把每一個部門重新繫回中心。小人偶分布在它們之間的路徑上。這片地景暗示，一座城市就像一塊電路板，所依賴的不是任何單一建築，而是連結的連續。
